column1: # boru Language Specification: generic functions — gen [...] fn [...]
# Format: input<TAB>expected<TAB>description
# `def idg gen [T] fn [[x:T] [T] [x]]` declares a generic FUNCTION:
# the placeholders are live while the signature parses (so `x:T`,
# `xs:[:T]`, `m:{:T}` and the return list resolve), and at each CALL
# the parameters bind from the actual arguments' types (§9.2.2):
# a `x:T` slot binds typeof(arg); a `[:T]`/`{:T}` pattern binds the
# union of the element types (tor-merge — runtime calls are never
# rejected for parameter inconsistency). The bindings are installed
# in the per-call scope, so body-internal `of [T]` / `make (Box of
# [T])` resolve, and torn down with the body's locals. Bounds reject
# at dispatch (no matching signature) and at the return check.
# See design/legacy/GENERICS.10.ignore.
# §1  basics — one definition, every type
def idg gen [T] fn [[x:T] [T] [x]] end idg 5
column3: a generic identity passes an Integer through

column1: def idg gen [T] fn [[x:T] [T] [x]] end idg "hi"
column3: …and a String — one definition serves every type

column1: def idg gen [T] fn [[x:T] [T] [x]] end typeof (idg "hi")
column3: T binds typeof(arg) — consistent with the language's own typeof

column1: def second gen [K V] fn [[k:K v:V] [V] [v]] end second a/q 42
column3: two parameters bind independently

column1: def second gen [K V] fn [[k:K v:V] [V] [v]] end typeof (second a/q 42)
column3: …each from its own argument

column1: # §2  mirror call forms — forward / stack / mixed dispatch identically
def pick2 gen [T] fn [[a:T b:T] [T] [a]] end pick2 1 2
column3: forward form

column1: def pick2 gen [T] fn [[a:T b:T] [T] [a]] end 2 pick2 1
column3: infix form binds sig[0] forward, sig[1] from the stack

column1: def pick2 gen [T] fn [[a:T b:T] [T] [a]] end 2 1 pick2
column3: stack form is mirror-equivalent

column1: # §3  element binding — [:T] and {:T} patterns
def first1 gen [T] fn [[xs:[:T]] [T] [xs get 0]] end first1 [10 20 30]
column3: a typed-list param dispatches on a concrete list

column1: def first1 gen [T] fn [[xs:[:T]] [T] [xs get 0]] end first1 ["a" "b"]
column3: …for any element type

column1: def first1 gen [T] fn [[xs:[:T]] [T] [xs get 0]] end first1 [1 "x"]
column3: mixed elements tor-merge into T — never rejected at runtime

column1: def vals1 gen [T] fn [[m:{:T}] [T] [m dot a/q]] end vals1 {a:1 b:2}
column3: a typed-map param dispatches on a concrete map

column1: # §4  body-internal bindings — of [T] resolves per call
def Box gen [T] class {value:T} def boxit gen [T] fn [[x:T] [Any] [make (Box of [T]) {value:x}]] end typeof (boxit 42)
column3: the call's T binding reaches a body-internal instantiation

column1: def Box gen [T] class {value:T} def boxfirst gen [T] fn [[xs:[:T]] [Any] [make (Box of [T]) {value:(xs get 0)}]] end typeof (boxfirst [1 2 3])
column3: …including T inferred from list elements

column1: def Pair gen [K V] refine Record [key:K value:V] def pairup gen [K V] fn [[k:K v:V] [Any] [make (Pair of [K V]) {key:k value:v}]] end pairup a/q 1
column3: multi-parameter bindings reach a record instantiation

column1: # §5  bounds — reject at dispatch and at return
def bnd gen [(T extends Number)] fn [[x:T] [T] [x]] end bnd 5
column3: a lattice bound admits a subtype

column1: def bnd gen [(T extends Number)] fn [[x:T] [T] [x]] end bnd 1.5
column3: …any subtype

column1: def bnd gen [(T extends Number)] fn [[x:T] [T] [x]] end bnd "no"
column3: …and rejects a non-member at dispatch

column1: def summit gen [(T extends Number)] fn [[xs:[:T]] [T] [xs get 0]] end summit [1 2 3]
column3: a bounded [:T] param admits a conforming list

column1: def summit gen [(T extends Number)] fn [[xs:[:T]] [T] [xs get 0]] end summit ["x" "y"]
column3: …and rejects off-bound elements at dispatch

column1: def badret gen [(T extends Number)] fn [[x:T] [T] ["oops"]] end badret 5
column3: the return check enforces the bound (the message names the parameter)

column1: # §6  recursion + closures
def repeat gen [T] fn [[x:T n:Integer] [Integer] [if (n lte 0) [0] [1 add (repeat x (n sub 1))]]] end repeat "a" 3
column3: a generic fn calls itself

column1: def mka gen [T] fn [[x:T] [Function] [fn [[y:Integer] [Integer] [x add y]]]] def add5 (mka 5) end add5 3
column3: an inner fn captures a generic fn's param

column1: # §7  higher-order composition — instantiation lists through each/fold
def Box gen [T] class {value:T} def xs [(make (Box of [Integer]) {value:10}) (make (Box of [Integer]) {value:20})] end xs each [dot value]
column3: each iterates instantiation instances precisely

column1: def Box gen [T] class {value:T} def xs [(make (Box of [Integer]) {value:10}) (make (Box of [Integer]) {value:20})] end 0 fold [dot value add] xs
column3: fold reduces over them

column1: def Box gen [T] class {value:T} def unbox gen [T] fn [[b:T] [Any] [b dot value]] end [(make (Box of [Integer]) {value:1})] each [unbox]
column3: a generic fn works as a higher-order body

column1: def Box gen [T] class {value:T} def sumvals gen [T] fn [[bs:[:T]] [Integer] [0 fold [dot value add] bs]] def xs [(make (Box of [Integer]) {value:10}) (make (Box of [Integer]) {value:20})] end sumvals xs
column3: a [:T] param accepts a DEF-BOUND list (the forward pattern check resolves word args)

column1: def f2 fn [[xs:[:Integer]] [Integer] [xs size]] def zs [1 2] end f2 zs
column3: …the same fix for plain typed-list params (was literal-only)

column1: # §8  hygiene — bindings never leak; loose unbound return is pinned
def idg gen [T] fn [[x:T] [T] [x]] def r (idg 5) end T
column3: the per-call T binding tears down with the body's locals

column1: def loose gen [T] fn [[x:Integer] [T] [x]] end loose 1
column3: an unbindable UNCONSTRAINED parameter passes the loose runtime return check (the checker reports the precision loss — Phase 5)
